answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a bond locked in a public contract, then slash that bond when an identity is proven to have double-claimed a reward. The rule makes a sybil attack costly: creating many identities ties up capital, and detected fraud burns it rather than merely losing a free account. A lagoon community might set the bond at a summit, but raising it too high excludes honest newcomers; calibrating it limits the spiral of abuse without making entry prohibitive.
